| `tls-grease` | DISABLED_BY_PATCH | **INVESTIGATE** | #10 → **#20** | `none` | Changing TLS handshake behaviour makes Astro fingerprintable in a new way while removing one form of ossification protection. Security-relevant capabilities are #20's decision. This entry exists so the matrix is complete and so the capability is routed rather than forgotten; it is deliberately not classified here. |
| `trk-scheme-blocking` | DISABLED_BY_PATCH | **REPLACE** | #8 | `none` | The mechanism that makes 51 Google endpoint literals unreachable while leaving their calling code compiled and reachable. It is a net-layer backstop standing in for build configuration, and it is the reason so many hosts in the endpoint manifest are DISABLE_RUNTIME rather than DISABLE_BUILD. REPLACE: the property survives — Astro contacts none of those hosts — the mechanism does not, because #8 removes patch-based construction and a URL-rewriting backstop is not a build configuration. |

Security-relevant capabilities are #20's decision. This entry exists so the matrix is complete and so the capability is routed rather than forgotten; it is deliberately not classified here. |

## Decisions that block another issue

| Feature | Blocks | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `alia` | #11 | #11 must enumerate which internal pages exist and which are trusted (astro://) versus isolated (astro-untrusted://). That list is this set, so the trust model cannot be written without it. |
| `astro-adblock-webui` | #11 | One more internal page the scheme's host list must account for. |
| `astro-error-page` | #11 | #11 must enumerate which internal pages exist and which are trusted (astro://) versus isolated (astro-untrusted://). That list is this set, so the trust model cannot be written without it. |
| `astro-newtab` | #11 | #11 must enumerate which internal pages exist and which are trusted (astro://) versus isolated (astro-untrusted://). That list is this set, so the trust model cannot be written without it. |
| `astro-settings` | #11 | #11 must enumerate which internal pages exist and which are trusted (astro://) versus isolated (astro-untrusted://). That list is this set, so the trust model cannot be written without it. |
| `astro-whats-new` | #11 | #11 must enumerate which internal pages exist and which are trusted (astro://) versus isolated (astro-untrusted://). That list is this set, so the trust model cannot be written without it. |
| `first-run-page` | #11 | It is an internal WebUI host, so it belongs in the scheme's page inventory. |
| `oxy-identity` | #11 | The callback is astro://auth/callback (oxy_auth_service.h:22-23). Whether a remote origin may navigate to the trusted scheme is a scheme trust-model axiom, and the answer decides whether this flow can exist in its current shape at all. #11 must state it explicitly rather than leave it implied. |
| `webui-csp-and-trusted-types` | #11 | What a trusted astro:// document may execute is part of the scheme's trust model, not a per-page choice. #11 has to fix the floor before #14 packages pages onto it. |
| `webui-fonts` | #11, #14 | #11 sets the baseline CSP for the trusted scheme. A scheme designed around a font host it must reach has a materially weaker model than one that may not reach the network at all, and the epic forbids the former outright. |
| `astro-internal-schemes` | #12, #13 | Everything downstream of the scheme depends on this decision being taken first, which is why the epic orders #11 → #12 → #13. |
